summary: The whole specimen is one 80-column <pre> of ASCII art set in Jgs, a pixel font family whose glyphs join across characters and lines: a text-mode wordmark, short notes, then figures that go from joining primitives (textures, curves, slopes) to patterns, faces, an interior, a landscape and an isometric city. Three ASCII '[X]' switches at the top re-render the entire page in jgs5/7/9, at ×1/×2/×3 and in day or night mode.

instances.look: First line of the page, written as text: 'Font [ ] jgs5 [X] jgs7 [ ] jgs9 · Size [ ] * 1 [X] * 2 [ ] * 3 · Mode [X] Day [ ] Night', blue link labels with a ===== rule beneath
instances.ux: Each '[ ]' is a link that sets a class on <body> (jgs5|jgs7|jgs9, x1|x2|x3, day|night): the whole page, art included, re-renders in that font, pixel multiple or colour scheme; the X moves to the chosen option
instances.learn: Build the switches out of the font's own characters ('[X]' radio buttons) and let them restyle every figure on the page: the specimen tests itself

reconstruction.layout: Three label groups in one 80-column pre line, at columns 0, 30 and 57 (x≈8, ≈430, ≈810px at 14px per column); labels above on the previous line; full-width '=' rule under it
reconstruction.typography: Everything in Jgs7 at 28px (×2), 14px column advance, 28px line pitch; links #0000ee-ish blue, text black
reconstruction.behaviour: Click → script swaps body classes; CSS maps jgs5 → 10/20/30px, jgs7 → 14/28/42px, jgs9 → 18/36/54px so joins stay pixel-exact; Night inverts to light-on-dark

instances.look: 'JGS FONT' as a figlet-style ASCII-art wordmark of underscores and pipes, which the font joins into unbroken outline letters, framed by double '=' rules; below it 'X Download Jgs Font (SIL Open Font License)' and 'FR Version française'
instances.ux: Download link and language switch under the wordmark
instances.learn: Draw the name with ordinary characters (_ | /): if the font makes them join, the wordmark itself proves the font's trick

reconstruction.layout: Four pre lines of ASCII art, centred-ish from column ~17 to ~63 (~650px wide, ~110px tall), between two pairs of full-width '=' rules (~1130px); link lines below
reconstruction.typography: Jgs7 28px; the wordmark's strokes come from '_' and '|' that meet at cell edges
reconstruction.content: Name as ASCII art; download and French-version links

instances.look: One line 'X Download Jgs Font (SIL Open Font License)' right under the wordmark
instances.ux: Links to the ZIP of the Velvetyne GitLab repository; the licence is named inline
instances.learn: For a free font, one download line with the licence name in brackets is enough

instances.look: Short paragraphs in the pre: a tribute to Joan G. Stark (jgs, ASCII-art pioneer), how glyphs combine into continuous lines, and why there are three fonts (Jgs5/7/9 for size multiples of 10/14/18 px); then an underlined 'Notes' heading saying the project is unfinished, with a link to a character table
instances.ux: Link to jgs_table.html (character table and comparison between the fonts)
instances.learn: State the pixel-size rule (multiples of 10/14/18) up front: it is the one thing users must know to keep the joins intact

reconstruction.layout: 80-column pre, left aligned, ~1130px wide; blank lines between paragraphs; headings underlined with '-----'
reconstruction.content: 'Jgs Font is a font family made in tribute to Joan G. Stark (aka jgs, Spunk), a pioneer of ASCII art… Jgs5 for sizes multiples of 10: 10px, 20px, 30px etc.'

instances.look: 'Continuous characters': a 4-column grid of ~18×8-character tiles, each one character repeated (. : / % - = | # ~ x …) so it fuses into a seamless texture: dots, hatching, lines, grids, diamonds, waves, scales and solid tones
instances.learn: Fill a tile with one repeated character: whether the texture is seamless shows the joining design better than any explanation

reconstruction.layout: Tiles 18 columns × ~8 lines (~250×225px), 2-column gutters, 4 per row, ~6 rows
reconstruction.typography: Jgs7 28px; the textures come from the glyphs touching the cell edges
reconstruction.content: Every joining character repeated as a block

instances.look: 'Curves': sine waves drawn with . - ~ ' characters at amplitudes labelled 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.25, 2.25, 4.25; 'Lines': a fan of straight lines drawn with characters at slopes labelled 0/1, 1/6, 1/4, 2/5 … 4/1, 9/2
instances.learn: Label each drawn curve or slope with its ratio: the specimen becomes a reference for which character combinations give which angle

reconstruction.layout: Curves: one wave per row, ~1130px wide, labels at the left; Lines: slope labels in one header row, lines descending ~12 rows below from each label
reconstruction.typography: Jgs7 28px; labels in the same font
reconstruction.content: Wave amplitudes and line slopes as numeric labels

instances.look: A run of full-width ASCII-art figures, each under a small underlined heading: 'Alphabet' (A–Z as blocky outline letters), 'Patterns' (border bands and lattices), 'Faces' (nine portraits with glasses, hats, curly hair), 'Interior' (a room with furniture), 'Landscape' (clouds, hills, forest, cyclists) and 'Isometric view' (a city with buildings, signs, cars and a bus), signed 'adl'
instances.ux: static; scrolling reveals ever more complex scenes; everything re-renders when the toolbar changes font, size or mode
instances.learn: Order the figures from primitives to full scenes: the visitor learns the building blocks, then sees what they add up to

reconstruction.layout: Each figure 80 columns wide (~1130px) left-aligned; heights from ~2 lines (alphabet, ~110px) to ~70 lines (isometric city, ~1900px); ~3 blank lines between figures
reconstruction.typography: All Jgs7 28px, one colour; headings same size underlined with '-'
reconstruction.content: Original ASCII artworks by the designer (faces, interior, landscape, isometric street scene)
reconstruction.assets: none: all artwork is text in the pre
